chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Isma'il from his father who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man upon whom death descended, so he made a bequest to his son and two brothers. The son witnessed his will, but the two brothers were absent. After some days, they refused to accept the bequest, fearing that his son would seize [the estate] from them, and they were unable to do what was proper. So a cousin of theirs, who was obeyed by them, guaranteed on their behalf that he would suffice them with his son. They entered [the arrangement] with this condition, but he did not suffice them with his son, although they had stipulated his son for them. And they said: 'We are free from the bequest, and we are in release from leaving all things and exiting from it.' [The Imam] said: 'It is binding upon you, so be gentle in whatever manner, for you will be rewarded, and perhaps that will suffice for his son.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if heirs refuse to accept a bequest to avoid sharing the estate with the designated beneficiary?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) addresses the legal nuance of conditional bequests (*wasiyya*) where heirs attempt to evade responsibility by substituting a guarantor. The Imam affirms that the original obligation remains binding upon the two brothers, emphasizing that fulfilling the bequest with gentleness (*furq*) ensures spiritual reward and potentially resolves the nephew's claim, thereby preserving family harmony and legal integrity.
